Statement of Investment Policy

ANCHORAGE POLICE AND FIRE RETIREMENT SYSTEM 
STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY
FOREWORD
The Anchorage Police and Fire Retirement System (APFRS) was created by the 
Anchorage Municipal Assembly by ordinance in 1977 (AO No.77-205; AO No. 84-69; 
AO No. 2000-65, § 3, 4-18-00). Police and Fire employees hired July 1, 1968 or later 
retroactively became members in the retirement plan. 
The system is comprised of three retirement plans, all of which were created for the 
purpose of encouraging qualified personnel to enter and remain in the service of the 
Municipality of Anchorage as police officers and firefighters through the establishment 
of a system of retirement, disability and death benefits for members, and their 
beneficiaries. The retirement plans are closed with Plan I closing to new members 
effective June 30, 1977, Plan II closing to new members effective April 17, 1984, and 
Plan III closing to new members effective May 24, 1994 for new command police and 
fire, July 17, 1994 for union firefighters and all new union police officers
October 5, 1994. 
A nine member Board of Trustees governs APFRS. The Board has sole and exclusive 
fiduciary responsibility over the assets of the retirement system. The Board has the sole 
and exclusive responsibility to administer APFRS in a manner that will assure prompt 
delivery of benefits and related services to the members and their beneficiaries.
The APFRS Director has the responsibility for the overall management and 
administration of the system in accordance with the direction, policy and goals set by the 
Board and Anchorage Municipal Code. Reporting to the Director is a staff with the 
primary responsibility to assist the Director to carry out these policies and goals.
An annual actuarial valuation commissioned by the Board determines contributions into 
the APFRS Plans. The growth of the Fund results from a combination of employer and 
employee contributions plus investment gains, less the combination of administrative 
costs, investment expenses, and benefit payments. The Retirement System is also subject 
to an annual outside audit commissioned by the Board. The results of the actuarial 
valuation and audit are provided to the Board, Municipal Executives, and Assembly.

3 
THE PURPOSE OF THE INVESTMENT POLICY AND OBJECTIVES:
1. Articulate the Board’s views on APFRS’ investment objectives and risk tolerance 
for the investment portfolio. 
2. Establish performance standards to measure the progress towards achieving the 
objectives.
3. Formulate the Board’s policies and guidelines on: a) asset allocation and 
diversification of investments; b) allowable investments; c) rebalancing; d) 
implementing policy-based initiatives; e) monitoring and evaluating the 
performance and risk of the investment portfolio; and f) investment manager 
selection and termination.
I.
1. 
INVESTMENT GOAL:
Provide for present and future benefit payments including increased benefits should reserves 
exceed 116%. The overall purpose is to invest pension assets, solely in the interest of providing
benefits to the members and their beneficiaries, attempting to minimize the employer and 
employee contributions and defraying administrative costs. The investment of the fund assets 
made in accordance with the investment policy described herein are expected to accomplish the 
goal of maintaining adequate funding of AFPRS’ liabilities over time.
The goal of the Board is to design an investment portfolio that will achieve an actuarial rate of 
return assumption of 6.90%. 
2. Make Prudent Investments – With care, skill, prudence and diligence the Board 
will strive to produce an investment return based on levels of liquidity and 
investment risk that are prudent and reasonable under present circumstances. 
Such circumstances may change over time.
3. Diversify the Assets – The Board will diversify the investments of the Fund to 
maximize the investment return within acceptable investment risk. 
4. Establish policy and review process – Annually, APFRS will conduct a 
formal review of its Investment Policy and will consider long term financial 
projections prepared by the Investment Consultant. 
II. INVESTMENT PHILOSOPHY:
In general, research has shown that the level of investment return is related to the 
corresponding level of investment risk. To achieve the actuarial target earning 
goal, the Board has adopted a long-term strategic asset allocation plan. APFRS 
will utilize some level of active investment management strategy to provide 
additional return required to achieve the target earnings rate. The Board strives

to seek a balance between the certainties of obtaining a set return over time with
the risks inherent in higher investment returns. The Board may employ lower 
cost and lower risk strategies to achieve its stated earnings goals 
III. INVESTMENT OBJECTIVES:
It is in the best interest of the Retirement System that investment objectives be 
established by the Board for the total fund and for each investment manager. It is 
clearly understood that these objectives are to be viewed over the long-term and 
have been established after full consideration of all factors set out in this 
Statement of Investment Policy (“SIP”). The investment objectives are as 
follows: 
A. Total Fund Investment Objectives
1. To achieve a minimum return of 5.0% in excess of the U.S. City 
Average, All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) as reported by the Bureau of 
Labor Statistics. However, the return shall be no less than the stated 
return the actuary utilizes in determining future normal benefit costs.
2. Exceed the return of a custom index, based on the target asset mix 
specified in Section V.D.
3. The Board shall strive to achieve a level of 116% funding (the 
Contingency Reserve) of the retirement system’s pension benefit 
liability in each Plan over time. Also, in each Plan, the Board will 
annually set aside 25% of any identified surpluses as an additional 
contingency reserve as required by Municipal Code. The Board has 
the authority with a simple majority vote to distribute the surplus in 
accordance with AMC 3.85. 
4. Surpluses above the additional contingency reserve may be available
for enhanced benefits only upon concurrence and recommendation of 
the Board's actuary and approval by a Super-Majority of the 
Retirement Board and by ordinance approved by the Anchorage 
Assembly. 
B. The Investment Managers Agreement may also contain additional 
investment performance objectives and goals for performance monitoring. 
IV. BOARD AND CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITIES:
The Board, under the Anchorage Municipal Code Chapter 3.85, is responsible for 
the establishment of investment policies that guide investment of the Anchorage 
Police and Fire Retirement System assets. As such:
A. The Board Shall determine the appropriate investment policies by 
considering the implications of a wide range of financial assumptions and

investment risk; 
B. The Board is the sole authority for hiring, retaining, and releasing 
managers, investment consultant and the master custodian; 
C. The managers shall be responsible to the Board for carrying out the 
Board’s investment goals, objectives and policies; 
D. The managers are accorded full discretion, within investment policy 
limits, to select individual securities and diversify assets under their 
control. Manager discretion may also be limited by the terms of the 
investment management agreement between the System and the 
manager;
E. The master custodian shall be responsible for safekeeping assets under the 
master custodian’s supervision and shall be responsible for administering 
any Securities Lending Agreement between the Board and the bank; 
F. The Director shall be responsible for implementing the Board’s 
investment policies, monitoring the managers and master custodian, and 
deploying assets within the established asset allocation parameters.
G. The Investment Consultant shall review and evaluate the performance of 
investment managers for APFRS and provide written quarterly reports and 
advice to the Board. The Investment Consultant shall attend regular 
periodic meetings and make oral presentations regarding the investment 
managers’ performance during each period. The Investment Consultant 
shall conduct an annual review of APFRS investment objectives, 
guidelines and procedures and, if necessary, make recommendations for 
amendments thereto. When necessary, assist the Board with interim 
changes to the System’s Asset Allocation Policy when managers are either 
added or deleted.
V. INVESTMENT POLICIES:
A. Actuarially Required Return
The assets of the Anchorage Police and Fire Retirement System shall be 
invested to provide an actuarially required return on investment within
acceptable risk parameters, as specified in V.C.4 below, (Acceptable 
Investment Risk). 
B. Prudent Person Rule

The Board of Trustees is by law collectively and individually, considered 
to be fiduciaries of the System and shall discharge its responsibilities 
solely in the interest of the members and beneficiaries of the System for 
the exclusive purpose of providing benefits to the members and their 
beneficiaries and to defray the reasonable expenses of the System. The 
Trustees shall exercise those fiduciary responsibilities with the care, skill, 
prudence and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a 
prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters 
would use in the conduct of an enterprise of a similar character and with 
similar aims.
C. Asset Allocation Factors
The Board shall carefully consider the following factors in establishing a 
long-term asset allocation program:
1. Retirement System Characteristics:
a. The system is a public system with tax-exempt status, and 
investments shall be made in a fiduciary responsible manner for 
the benefit of the membership.
b. It is understood by the Board that member and municipal 
contributions may be required from time to time. However, the 
primary source of revenue for benefit payments is from investment 
earnings on the Retirement System’s assets.
c. Plan member demographics and nature of the Plans’ liabilities will 
be considered when developing an investment strategy. 
Additionally with APFRS being a closed system, the Board will 
take into consideration time horizons and invest in more 
conservative investments over time. 
2. Liquidity Requirements:
The System’s assets shall be structured to meet the liquidity 
requirements to pay benefits in a timely manner. Accordingly, the 
managers should be prepared to provide assets to meet liquidity 
requirements as the need arises. In addition, investment manager fees 
benefit payments and expenses will, at the discretion of the Director, 
be deducted directly from all portfolios. It is important that each 
manager maintain sufficient liquidity to cover these periodic 
withdrawals.
3. Quarterly Allocation Rebalancing:
The Director, in conjunction with the Fund’s Investment Consultant, 
will review the asset allocation quarterly and compare it to the 
recommended target allocation. When one particular manager’s 
portfolio is over-weighted versus their target allocation, the Director, 
after coordinating with the Investment Consultant, may reallocate the

“overage” required by the allocation model and report that activity to 
the Board at the next ensuing meeting. An ongoing exception is 
made for alternative asset classes, which may differ from the target 
ranges outlined for periods of time, due to the illiquid nature of the 
asset classes. In the event the existing allocation is within the
maximum/minimum guidelines (see V. D. below) no action may be 
taken.
The Board will review the overall fund allocation of assets at their 
annual review meeting. Significantly over-weighted asset classes may 
be cut back at that time, particularly those which fall outside the 
guideline allocations. Otherwise, the Board will rely on the advice of 
the Investment Consultant for changes to weightings or to the Asset 
Allocation model.
4. Acceptable Investment Risk:
The aggregate risk level appropriate for the retirement system is 
specified in this investment policy statement, which reflects the Fund’s 
characteristics, and liquidity requirements, keeping in mind the 
fiduciary purpose for which the assets are accumulated. The 
acceptable risk level is specified in Section V. D.
5. Asset Allocation Studies:
Periodic asset allocation studies may be considered annually by the 
Board which will:
a. Develop a long range rationale to guide the deployment of 
contributions and assets;
b. Identify appropriate expected risk/return parameters for the 
investment of System assets; and
c. Reassess the current investment policy as it pertains to the 
relationship between the System’s assets and liabilities.
6. Capital Market Assumptions:
Capital market assumptions are reviewed annually by the Board and the 
Investment Consultant. 
D. Asset Allocation Program
After careful consideration of the above referenced asset allocation 
factors, the Board has established a long-term asset allocation program 
that leads to an appropriate asset mix, realistic investment objectives and 
relevant investment constraints, as summarized on the next page:

E. Minimum Manager Requirements:
In order to be considered as a manager for the system a firm must meet the 
following minimum standards:
1. The firm must have at least $500 million under management;
2. The firm’s portfolio must have a 5-year investment 
performance history.
F. Manager Guidelines:
1. Managers shall have full discretionary authority in the selection 
and retention of investments, subject to the provision of law, trust 
agreements, this Statement of Investment Policy as amended from 
time to time and investment management agreement between the 
System and the manager.
2. The responsibility for security selection shall lie with the managers.
The managers, however, shall operate within these investment 
guidelines which shall conform to applicable governmental 
regulations, and shall cover four specific areas: (a) diversification; 
(b) credit quality; (c) restricted transactions; and (d) exceptions.
a. Diversification:
(1) No individual security of the portfolio shall
constitute more than the greater of 5% or the 
security’s weight in the agreed upon market index 
plus 2%. Other exceptions to this provision may be 
requested as provided below in section (d).
(2) No security shall be bought unless it is traded on
one of the major security exchanges or the Over-The-Counter (OTC) market. Listed American
Depository Receipts (ADR’s) shall be an approved
investment, and shall constitute no more than 20% of 
the market value of the assets controlled by a 
manager.
(3) Exchange listed derivatives may be included in a 
manager’s portfolio. The manager is required to provide
the Board with a list and explanation of the types of
derivatives they expect to invest in, the purposes for
holding these securities in their portfolio, the likely
portfolio percentage allocation to derivatives and a 
description of the risks associated with these 
investments. Collateralized mortgage securities or
mortgage-backed securities are authorized by the Board,

10
but individual issues must have a Flow Uncertainty
Index (“FLUX”) score of 15 or less.
b. Credit quality:
(1) Commercial paper must be rated P-1 and/or A-1 by
Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s respectively.
(2) The total bond portfolio will maintain a minimum 
average credit rating of “BBB+” as rated by both 
Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s. For Purposes of
compliance with this Policy, the manager will 
adhere to the same ratings scale and policy as that 
employed by Bloomberg in the structure of the 
Bloomberg US Aggregate Index (utilizing ratings by 
Moody’s, S & P and Fitch).
c. Portfolio Duration:
Total portfolio weighted average duration should not
exceed 120% of the bond market’s duration utilizing the
Bloomberg US Aggregate Index.
d. Restricted transactions:
(1) Conflict of interest and transactions between a
fiduciary and parties in interest, as described in
Sections 406 and 408 of Title I, Employee 
Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA), are 
prohibited which provisions are adopted for use in 
this System.
(2) No transactions shall be made which might 
threaten the tax exempt status of the system.
(3) No letter stocks shall be purchased.
(4) No funds shall be borrowed.
(5) No short sales shall be made.
(6) No tax-exempt bond shall be purchased or retained
unless, on a comparable quality and duration basis, it
provides an expected return superior to that of a 
taxable bond.
(7) No private placements shall be purchased. 
However, Rule 144A securities with registration 
rights are permitted investments.
(8) No non-exchange-listed derivatives shall be
purchased or sold by any of the System’s managers.

11
e. Exceptions to Manager Guidelines:
(9) The Board acknowledges that when it is in the best
interests of the System to invest in a collective 
vehicle (i.e. comingled fund or mutual fund); it is 
not possible to dictate specific investment 
prohibitions. Therefore, it shall be the duty of the 
manager of such commingled fund to report to the 
Board on a periodic basis, the extent to which the 
investment strategies differ from the Board’s SIP.
Periodically, the Board will review the differences 
and determine if the commingled fund remains in 
the best interest of the System.
(10) The managers may request exceptions to the
restrictions outlined in V.F.2. by written
request to the Board.
(11) All exceptions will be submitted in writing to the
Board who will, after reviewing and receiving 
advice from the Fund’s Investment Consultant,
render a decision with regard to the request at the
next board meeting.
3. Brokerage Transactions
The managers shall purchase or sell securities through those firms 
offering the best price and execution. The Board reserves the right
to institute a Brokerage Recapture Program or to use the services of 
a “Transition Management” brokerage firm if the Board believes 
this is in the best interest. The decision to use a third party will be
based on advice and recommendations from the Board’s Investment 
Consultant.

12
G. MANAGER PERFORMANCE STANDARDS
Over the long-term (as defined in the following paragraph) each manager retained 
to actively manage a portfolio will be expected to outperform on a net of fee basis 
an appropriately defined and mutually agreed upon market index and to perform 
(gross of fees) in the top two-fifths (2/5) of managers with similar investment 
styles as measured by one of the prevailing investment performance measurement 
services.
The time period for measuring manager performance is a market cycle or three to 
five years, whichever period is shorter. However, if a manager experiences 
significant organizational changes and/or its performance falls significantly below 
market averages, the performance of a group of managers of similar style, and its 
individual performance objectives prior to completion of a market cycle, then the 
manager’s performance will be evaluated over a shorter time horizon. Over the 
life of the portfolio, each manager is expected to maintain a portfolio with 
consistent fundamental portfolio characteristics.
H. MONITORING AND EVALUATING MANAGER PERFORMANCE
The monitoring and evaluating the total fund and individual managers’ 
performance will be performed by an Investment Consultant. The objective and 
purpose of this monitoring is to maintain adequate control over the System’s 
assets and the managers without stifling their initiative. The Board shall conduct 
a formal evaluation of each manager’s performance quarterly. These evaluations 
will focus on adherence to investment policies and the opportunities available in 
the investment markets. Particular attention will be directed to evaluating 
performance relative to risk; this will be achieved by comparing individual 
managers and total Fund performance on a risk-adjusted basis. It is believed that 
the performance expectations set forth in this SIP are reasonable and consistent in 
the long run. 
Actions to be taken as a result of performance reviews will be in accordance with 
the Retirement Board’s Investment Monitoring and Transition Process Procedure 
in Exhibit A. Notwithstanding the performance measures in Exhibit A, the Board 
retains the authority to terminate any manager whenever it is deemed, in the 
Board’s exercise of its fiduciary duty, to be in the best interest of the System and 
its participants.

13
I. ADOPTION
This Statement of Investment Policy is adopted effective April 18, 2000, the date 
the revised Anchorage Municipal Code, Chapter 3.85 (Re-established), was 
approved by the Municipal Assembly. (See the “Document History” on the 
attached Page.)

SECTION ONE - FUNDING APPROACH 
1.1 Funding Approach in General
COAERS is an actuarial determined contribution (ADC) rate plan in which, each year, the actuary 
determines the normal cost of the plan as a percentage of pay adjusting for the administrative 
expense and amortization of any gain/loss layers (“liability layers) established after December 
31, 2022. The total normal cost of the plan is then forecasted for the upcoming year. The 
forecasted normal cost is reduced by the employee contribution rate to yield the upcoming years’ 
employer contribution rate. An existing amortization schedule of fixed payments, called Legacy 
Liability payments, has also been created to retire the plan’s Unfunded Actuarial Accrued 
Liability. The plan sponsor is required by law to make the required Legacy Liability payments in 
addition to the employer’s contribution each year. 
COAERS’ strategic funding objective is to meet the long-term pension obligations promised to 
all members of the plan. To meet this objective, COAERS has put in place a set of policies and 
legislative requirements to:
1. Establish a fixed payment schedule to pay off the Unfunded Actuarial Accrued Liability 
(UAAL) over a fixed, closed 30-year period, known as the Legacy Liability.
2. Conduct annual actuarial valuations, which include a Risk Sharing Valuation Study
(RSVS), to determine the ADC rate for the upcoming year for the employers participating 
in the plan (See TX CIV ST Art. 6243n for a full description of the state statute detailing 
the Risk Sharing Valuation Study).
3. Monitor the employer’s contribution rate relative to the expected future trajectory of 
the rate, known as a corridor midpoint.
4. If the employer portion of the ADC exceeds the corridor maximum (5% of pay above the 
corridor midpoint), take action to increase employee contributions up to the 2%
maximum, and discuss future changes to the Plan if the ADC exceeds the employer and 
employee maximums.
5. Periodically conduct Actuarial Experience Studies to review and adopt the assumptions 
and methods used to determine the cost of the promised benefits. State law requires 
Experience Studies to perform no less than every five years. The last Experience Study 
was conducted as of December 31, 2024.
1.2 Actuarial Determined Contribution
COAERS is an actuarially determined contribution (ADC) rate plan. The ADC is comprised of the 
normal cost and the administrative expense assumption adjusted for the amortization of any 
liability layers expressed as a percentage of pay. COAERS uses the Entry Age Normal actuarial 
cost method to develop the normal cost for each benefit component – retirement, termination, 
disability, etc. The administrative expense assumption is currently .70% of pay. 
In determining the future contribution rate, the actuary also determines if any adjustments are 
needed for gains or losses by way of additional liability layers. Such layers have already been 
established for 2023 and 2024 and will continue to be calculated each subsequent year. Future

10
actuarial losses are converted to a percentage of payroll, amortized, and the layer added to the 
normal cost. Future actuarial gains are converted to a percentage of payroll, amortized, and the 
layer subtracted from the normal cost. Based upon the result, the actuary then projects the 
normal cost for the future upcoming calendar year, and the employee contribution rate is 
subtracted to yield the employer contribution rate for the upcoming year.
In addition, a model of future expected employer contribution rates has also been established to 
help COAERS determine a range of future acceptable employer contribution rates. An Initial Risk 
Sharing Valuation Study (RSVS) was performed as of December 31, 2022 establishing a 
contribution rate corridor. The corridor has a midpoint which is the expected future trajectory 
of the employer contribution rate. Additionally, a minimum and a maximum employer 
contribution rate were also set at 5% of pay above and 5% of pay below the midpoint. This 
corridor provides COAERS with a range of possible future employer contribution rates. The 
contribution corridor is used to trigger important subsequent events. First, if the ADC would 
cause the employer contribution rate to exceed the corridor’s maximum contribution rate, then 
the employee contribution rate will have to increase accordingly. The increase would be added 
to the 10% current employee contribution rate up to an additional 2% of payroll to cover the 
shortfall. Second, if ADC exceeds the additional 2% of pay from the employees, then COAERS 
and the City of Austin must enter into discussions to come up with a plan to address the funding 
and the expense of the Plan. Finally, if the ADC is lower than the corridor midpoint, the employer 
contribution will remain at the corridor midpoint so long as the funded ratio is below 90%.

1.4 Contribution Rate Corridor Midpoints, Maximums, and Minimums 2024 to 2053
1.5 Normal Cost Layers for Gains/Losses After 2022
Gains and losses realized after 2022, create new amortization layers adjusting the normal cost

year to retire the unfunded actuarial accrued liability. The entire schedule of Legacy Liability 
payments can be found at www.coaers.org/RFP.
1.7 Investments
As of March 31, 2025, COAERS held investments with fair value totaling $3.5 billion. The 
Board has found it prudent to diversify both across and within the major asset classes to
construct a portfolio that delivers strong compound returns on a long-term, risk-adjusted 
basis. The Board recently adopted a new strategic asset allocation as shown below. Note 
however, that it is expected to take some time to ramp up the private market’s elements of 
the new strategic asset allocation.

12
Investments are made with care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then 
prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would 
use in the conduct of an enterprise of a like character and with like aims. Funds of COAERS are 
invested solely in the interest of the membership and their beneficiaries, and for the exclusive 
purpose of providing benefits to such membership and their beneficiaries while defraying 
reasonable expenses of administering COAERS. 
The Board of Trustees has established an Investment Policy Statement and related guidelines for 
the administration of the investment program. Moreover, an Investment Committee has been 
chartered to assist the Board with research, recommendations, and monitoring of the investment 
portfolio. Investment consulting services are provided by the Meketa Investment Group and 
COAERS employs four professionals to oversee day-to-day implementation activities of the
investment portfolio. 
1.8 Experience Studies
COAERS believes that a periodic review of our actuarial assumptions is crucial to understanding 
and managing the cost of the benefits promised to members of COAERS. The use of outdated 
or inappropriate assumptions can result in understated costs which will lead to higher future
contribution rates; or overstated costs which place an unnecessary financial burden on the City 
of Austin and its employees. Accordingly, COAERS conducts experience studies every five years. 
During each experience study, each assumption is reviewed and compared to the actual 
experience of the plan with consideration of adding in a slight margin for adverse experience. 
Then the assumptions, as a whole, are reviewed for reasonableness and consistency. COAERS
recently reviewed its actuarial assumptions based on census data as of December 31, 2024. 
Certain key assumptions are listed below. A full discussion of the assumptions can be found in 
the Experience Study Report at www.coaers/RFP.

2.2 Annual Actuarial Valuation (Including a Risk Sharing Valuation Study)
a) Description of Work: 
1) Measurements using the following actuarial methods:
i) Entry Age Normal Cost method will be used to allocate the cost of accruing benefits 
as a level percentage of pay over the period from the member’s entry into the plan 
until termination or retirement;
ii) Five-year smoothing method asset method which recognizes 20% of the differences 
between expected and actual investment income in the current and each 
subsequent year, with offsetting unrecognized gains and losses immediately
recognized; and a
iii) A declining 30-year amortization period to determine the payments on new liability 
layers until reaching 20-years, thereafter, using closed 20-year layers. The aggregate 
funding period for the system is the weighted average of the amortization layers. 
The goal is to eliminate negative amortization as soon as possible, but negative 
amortization is expected to continue until the Legacy Liability payoff schedule 
reaches 20 years.

(5) Funded status of the Plan;
(6) Change in Assets;
(7) Actuarial Gains and Losses; 
(8) An assessment of Disclosure of Risk Associated with Measuring Pension 
Obligations
(9) Disclosure of Actuarial Methods and Assumptions

ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS 
Type of Entity
The City of Austin Employees’ Retirement System (COAERS) is a single employer governmental 
defined benefit retirement system originally established in 1941 by City ordinance and governed 
since 1991 by Texas statute (Vernon’s Ann.Texas Civ.St. Art. 6243n). COAERS is qualified under 
Section 401(a) of the Internal Revenue Code. 
COAERS Board of Trustees
The COAERS Board of Trustees is vested with the statutory power and responsibility for the 
proper and effective general administration, management, and operation of the retirement 
system for the exclusive benefit of its present and future members and beneficiaries. The Board 
consists of 11 members comprised of City of Austin officials, employees, retirees, and citizens.
Participating Employers
Two employers participate in the Plan, the City of Austin Texas with over 17,000 active and 
deferred members and 7,100 retirees and the City of Austin Employees Retirement System 
staff with 38 active and deferred members and 13 retirees. 
Authority for Actuarial Services 
The COAERS Board of Trustees has statutory authority for the selection of an actuary. The 
statute states the Board of Trustees shall designate an actuary who shall be the technical 
advisor of the retirement board regarding the maintenance and operations of the fund but 
not an investment advisor or fiduciary with respect to any investments of the fund. The 
statute directs the actuary to perform valuations of the assets and liabilities of the fund.
Actuarial Determine Contribution Plan
COAERS is an actuarial determined contribution (ADC) rate plan in which, each year, the 
actuary determines the normal cost of the plan as a percentage of pay adjusting for the 
administrative expense and any liability layers established after December 31, 2022. The 
total normal cost of the plan isthen forecasted for the upcoming year. The forecasted normal 
cost is reduced by the employee contribution rate to yield the upcoming years’ employer 
contribution rate. The statutory requirements for the plan, including the determination of 
the ADC, can be found in the COAERS statutes at TX CIV ST Art 6243n.

SECTION ONE - FUNDING APPROACH 
1.1 Funding Approach in General
COAERS is an actuarial determined contribution (ADC) rate plan in which, each year, the actuary 
determines the normal cost of the plan as a percentage of pay adjusting for the administrative 
expense and amortization of any gain/loss layers (“liability layers) established after December 
31, 2022. The total normal cost of the plan is then forecasted for the upcoming year. The 
forecasted normal cost is reduced by the employee contribution rate to yield the upcoming years’ 
employer contribution rate. An existing amortization schedule of fixed payments, called Legacy 
Liability payments, has also been created to retire the plan’s Unfunded Actuarial Accrued 
Liability. The plan sponsor is required by law to make the required Legacy Liability payments in 
addition to the employer’s contribution each year. 
COAERS’ strategic funding objective is to meet the long-term pension obligations promised to 
all members of the plan. To meet this objective, COAERS has put in place a set of policies and 
legislative requirements to:
1. Establish a fixed payment schedule to pay off the Unfunded Actuarial Accrued Liability 
(UAAL) over a fixed, closed 30-year period, known as the Legacy Liability.
2. Conduct annual actuarial valuations, which include a Risk Sharing Valuation Study
(RSVS), to determine the ADC rate for the upcoming year for the employers participating 
in the plan (See TX CIV ST Art. 6243n for a full description of the state statute detailing 
the Risk Sharing Valuation Study).
3. Monitor the employer’s contribution rate relative to the expected future trajectory of 
the rate, known as a corridor midpoint.
4. If the employer portion of the ADC exceeds the corridor maximum (5% of pay above the 
corridor midpoint), take action to increase employee contributions up to the 2%
maximum, and discuss future changes to the Plan if the ADC exceeds the employer and 
employee maximums.
5. Periodically conduct Actuarial Experience Studies to review and adopt the assumptions 
and methods used to determine the cost of the promised benefits. State law requires 
Experience Studies to perform no less than every five years. The last Experience Study 
was conducted as of December 31, 2024.
1.2 Actuarial Determined Contribution
COAERS is an actuarially determined contribution (ADC) rate plan. The ADC is comprised of the 
normal cost and the administrative expense assumption adjusted for the amortization of any 
liability layers expressed as a percentage of pay. COAERS uses the Entry Age Normal actuarial 
cost method to develop the normal cost for each benefit component – retirement, termination, 
disability, etc. The administrative expense assumption is currently .70% of pay. 
In determining the future contribution rate, the actuary also determines if any adjustments are 
needed for gains or losses by way of additional liability layers. Such layers have already been 
established for 2023 and 2024 and will continue to be calculated each subsequent year. Future

10
actuarial losses are converted to a percentage of payroll, amortized, and the layer added to the 
normal cost. Future actuarial gains are converted to a percentage of payroll, amortized, and the 
layer subtracted from the normal cost. Based upon the result, the actuary then projects the 
normal cost for the future upcoming calendar year, and the employee contribution rate is 
subtracted to yield the employer contribution rate for the upcoming year.
In addition, a model of future expected employer contribution rates has also been established to 
help COAERS determine a range of future acceptable employer contribution rates. An Initial Risk 
Sharing Valuation Study (RSVS) was performed as of December 31, 2022 establishing a 
contribution rate corridor. The corridor has a midpoint which is the expected future trajectory 
of the employer contribution rate. Additionally, a minimum and a maximum employer 
contribution rate were also set at 5% of pay above and 5% of pay below the midpoint. This 
corridor provides COAERS with a range of possible future employer contribution rates. The 
contribution corridor is used to trigger important subsequent events. First, if the ADC would 
cause the employer contribution rate to exceed the corridor’s maximum contribution rate, then 
the employee contribution rate will have to increase accordingly. The increase would be added 
to the 10% current employee contribution rate up to an additional 2% of payroll to cover the 
shortfall. Second, if ADC exceeds the additional 2% of pay from the employees, then COAERS 
and the City of Austin must enter into discussions to come up with a plan to address the funding 
and the expense of the Plan. Finally, if the ADC is lower than the corridor midpoint, the employer 
contribution will remain at the corridor midpoint so long as the funded ratio is below 90%.

1.8 Experience Studies
COAERS believes that a periodic review of our actuarial assumptions is crucial to understanding 
and managing the cost of the benefits promised to members of COAERS. The use of outdated 
or inappropriate assumptions can result in understated costs which will lead to higher future
contribution rates; or overstated costs which place an unnecessary financial burden on the City 
of Austin and its employees. Accordingly, COAERS conducts experience studies every five years. 
During each experience study, each assumption is reviewed and compared to the actual 
experience of the plan with consideration of adding in a slight margin for adverse experience. 
Then the assumptions, as a whole, are reviewed for reasonableness and consistency. COAERS
recently reviewed its actuarial assumptions based on census data as of December 31, 2024. 
Certain key assumptions are listed below. A full discussion of the assumptions can be found in 
the Experience Study Report at www.coaers/RFP.

Plan Administration RFP
3
GENERAL INFORMATION
Background
The Monroe County Deferred Compensation Plan (the Plan) is a defined contribution plan covering all 
the employees of the County of Monroe. The Plan is exempt from income taxes under Internal Revenue 
Service Section 457(b) of the Internal Revenue Code. The Plan is subject to the Rules and Regulations 
of the New York State Deferred Compensation Board, Parts 9000 to 9006 and operates off of the State 
Model Plan Document.
The purpose of the Plan is to provide employees with a convenient and efficient way to build long-term 
retirement savings and to encourage broad-based participation of employees in the plan as a 
supplemental retirement security tool to their State defined benefit pension and Social Security. The Plan 
wants to assure that this additional benefit be recognized by all employees, that they have the opportunity 
to receive one-on-one education and voluntarily participate.
The Plan also has an OBRA part time seasonal component.
As of December 31, 2022, the Plan had 4,398 plan participants with a Plan assets of $308,676,730. In 
addition the OBRA part-time seasonal plan had 536 participants with assets of $926,785. Contributions 
were $13,290,747 during the year, plus roll over inflow. The median account balance was $26,191. 
Additional Plan information is presented in Exhibit C. The County currently has approximately 4,100 full-time employees at any given time. The Plan is supported by one (1) full-time exclusive enroller/educator. 
He conducts approximately 100 group meetings and over 1,000 individual seminars.
County’s Objective
The County’s objectives in seeking to maintain such a plan for its employees are as follows:
1. To provide a means by which its employees can enhance their financial position and retirement 
income.
2. To provide a planned program that will facilitate their efforts to do so.
3. To provide a system for a social security compliance program for seasonal and part-time employment.
4. To provide consultation on an as-needed basis for review of financial hardship withdrawal.
5. To provide a trustee to meet trustee requirement as per the Rules and Regulations established by 
the New York State Deferred Compensation Board. 
6. To assist the Monroe County Deferred Compensation Committee in the performance of its duties 
under Section 41 of the Monroe County Code and to implement the decision of the committee.

Plan Administration RFP
4
Scope of Services
The Monroe County Deferred Compensation Plan Committee (the Committee) developed this Request 
For Proposals (RFP) to obtain proposals from qualified Administrative Service Agencies and/or Financial 
Organizations relating to (1) trust service, (2) administration and/or (3) funding of an "eligible deferred 
compensation plan.” If you are "qualified" according to the Regulations to administer, maintain records 
and accounts of plans and/or if you have appropriate trust services and/or products available for use as 
funding media and are interested in making those services and/or products available, you are requested 
to complete this RFP.
Submission of Proposal
1. Six (6) copies plus one original of the proposal should be submitted to the following address to arrive
no later than 3:00 p.m. on September 8, 2023:
Walter Webert, Contract Management Coordinator
Monroe County Deferred Compensation Committee
c/o County of Monroe
Office of Purchasing & Central Services
39 W. Main Street, Room 200
Rochester, NY 14614
2. Questions that arise during the proposal preparation process must be received in writing, or via e-mail, by Walter Webert no later than 3:00 P.M. on August 18, 2023 (e-mail: 
wwebert@monroecounty.gov). Questions and responses will be provided in the form of an addendum 
to the specifications which, if issued, will be conveyed via e-mail to all firms who received this RFP 
no later than the close of business August 25, 2023. No contact will be allowed between the firm and 
any other member of the Committee or County with regard to this RFP during the RFP process unless 
specifically authorized in writing by the Contract Management Coordinator or his designee. Prohibited 
contact may be grounds for firm disqualification.
3. Any proposals received after 3:00 p.m. on September 8, 2023 will not be considered. It is each 
Proposer’s responsibility to assure that proposals are shipped in a timely fashion so as to be received 
by the designated party on or before the due date. We accept no responsibility for lost and/or late 
delivery of proposals.
Form and Substance
The New York State Deferred Compensation Board has promulgated The "Rules and Regulations" 
(effective June 15, 2011), hereafter referred to as the "Regulations", and the Model Plan (including 
amendments through December 11, 2020) for which you are to rely on for responding to this RFP. These 
documents can be found at the following link: https://deferredcompboard.ny.gov
Failure to conform to or satisfy any requirement of these documents may result in the rejection of the 
proposal. 
1. Proposer must include a fully completed questionnaire, restating each statement or question in 
Section I through Section V inclusive, and by recording your response directly below each statement 
or question.

Plan Administration RFP
5
2. Proposers must respond to all questions in the "Contractual Requirements" section (Section I) and 
must conform to the specifications set forth in this RFP. If a question, statement or section does not 
apply, put “not applicable” as your response. If recordkeeping services are provided by a “person” 
(defined by the Regulations) that is neither the parent nor subsidiary company of the Financial 
Organization, then separate and complete responses must be provided by each company.
3. Proposer must include a transmittal letter on the Company's official letterhead signed by an official of 
the Company who is authorized to commit the organization to perform the services outlined in the 
submitted proposal: you must indicate such commitment. The transmittal letter must contain a 
representation that the proposal complies with all requirements of the Regulations and the Model 
Plan. 
4. By submitting a proposal, each Proposer agrees not to make any claims for or have any right to 
damages because of any misunderstanding or misrepresentation of specifications, because of any 
misinformation or lack of information or because such Proposer is not selected to provide the services 
proposed. Submission of a proposal constitutes express acceptance by the Proposer of all provisions 
of this RFP including all attachments.
5. By submitting a proposal, you agree to include in your contracts and agreements a provision that all 
commitments, representations, promises or claims made in your proposal documents or oral 
presentations are made part of any contract entered into with the Committee.
6. Costs of developing proposals, making presentations and any subsequent expenses relating to 
contract negotiation are entirely the responsibility of the Proposer and may not be charged to the 
County of Monroe or the plan participants.
7. In order to facilitate our analysis and evaluation of the proposals, it is essential that a uniform format 
be employed in their preparation. Therefore, the content and format of your proposal should follow 
the guidelines set forth in this RFP. All responses should be as concise as possible. Excessive 
submissions may be grounds for disqualification.
Evaluation Criteria
In selecting, we will use criteria which comply with the requirements of the Regulations, including Section 
9003.3(a)(1 through 7) of the Regulations.
All qualified proposals, sought in conjunction with the requirements of Section 9003.2 of the Regulations, 
will be evaluated and awards made to the Proposer or Proposers whose bid is determined to be in the 
best interest of the plan participants.
Selection Process
Section 9001.2(b) of the Regulations, recognizes that we have appointed a committee to act on our 
behalf, to the extent permitted or required by the Regulations and by the Model Plan. Section 9003.3(c): 
before any contract or agreement entered into by the committee may become effective, the committee 
must submit in writing, to the President of the New York State Civil Service Commission, the name of 
such selected Proposer(s) and a “certification” signed by the chief executive officer and chief legal officer 
stating that such Proposer(s) has been duly selected to provide services in accordance with provisions 
of the Regulations.

Plan Administration RFP
6
1. Contracts or agreements cannot be awarded before the expiration of ninety (90) days from date of 
our announcement publication in the State Register and local paper. 
2. Invitations may be made for oral presentations.
3. Any award of a contract or agreement as a result of this RFP will be made by written notification.
4. The projected timetable for the selection process will be as follows:
September 8, 2023 Deadline for submission of proposals
By September 29, 2023 Review of proposals
By October 27, 2023 Sub-committee selection
By November 9, 2023 Final Full Committee selection
January 1, 2024 Financial products and administrative Services 
implemented and operational
5. It is our policy to solicit proposals with a bona fide intention to award a contract. This policy 
notwithstanding, we reserve the right at any time to:
a. reject any or all proposals or parts thereof;
b. establish a deferred compensation plan by any of the methods prescribed by Section 
9001.2(a) of the Regulations
c. enter into direct negotiations with multiple proposers; and 
d. modify the selection procedure or the scope of the proposed project or of the required 
responses.
6. Soliciting proposals and granting of exclusive negotiation rights does not commit us to accept any of 
the terms of any proposal. Final terms of any agreement will be determined by direct negotiations 
and are subject to final approval by the County. We may suspend or terminate negotiations at any 
time that we determine additional negotiations would be unproductive.
Term of Contract
Pursuant to Section 9003.5(a) of the Regulations, we expect to enter into a written contractual 
arrangement(s) of up to five (5) years in duration. The contract shall be subject to periodic review by the 
Committee. The Committee may cancel the contract at the end of any contract year upon providing the 
investment management and/or the administrative services agency with 30 days advance notice in 
writing. All contracts and agreements entered into shall impose no penalties or surrender charges for 
the transfer of assets or responsibilities on expiration of the contract or agreement. Upon the expiration 
or termination of any contract(s) or agreement(s), the committee shall follow procedures set forth in the 
Regulations in Part 9003 for awarding new contracts and entering into new agreements.

Plan Administration RFP
7
SECTION I
CONTRACTUAL REQUIREMENTS
"Agree" or "Disagree" must be indicated for each of the following specifications. The following 
specifications can be found in either the Regulations or the Model Plan, all of which should have been 
enclosed as attachments. Please include reasons for any rejection or disagreement of any specification 
and alternative options, if applicable. There should be neither elaboration nor qualification for “agree” 
unless otherwise requested.
Specifications of the Regulations
1. Section 9000.2(b) - As a Financial Organization authorized to do business (provide investment 
products) in New York State, you agree that your firm is one of the following: (a) a Registered 
Investment Advisor, (b) a Bank or (c) an Insurance Company qualified under the laws of more than 
one state. 
2. If you are an Insurance Company acting through a subsidiary in New York State, then the Subsidiary 
Insurance Company must certify that it (the Subsidiary Insurance Company) is qualified to do 
business under the laws of more than one state.
3. Section 9001.2(b) - We have appointed a deferred compensation committee to act on our behalf and 
you agree to interface with this committee. Additionally, we may decide to be the grantor of our own 
trust, and then you also agree to interface with the trust and trustee: all funding contracts, of whatever 
nature, will be “issued to, owned and retained by the trustee”.
4. Section 9001.4(a) through (d) - You agree to abide by all four (4) provisions, especially not allowing 
annuity type payouts.
5. Section 9002.2(a)(5) - You will provide evidence that bonds and insurance have been secured by you 
pursuant to the Regulations.
6. Section 9002.2(a)(6) - You will acknowledge in writing that you will act as a fiduciary under Section 
457(g) of the Code and under State and common trust law principles with respect to all trusteeship, 
administrative, or investment matters for which you assume responsibility. Additionally, you agree to 
indemnify our Plan as a result of any cause of action brought against it as a result of acts or omissions 
together with the reasonable costs of litigation arising therefrom.
7. Section 9003.3(a) - Your proposal shall be in writing and contain a representation that the proposal 
complies with all requirements of the Regulations and clearly indicate all direct fees, indirect fees and 
charges.
8. Section 9003.5(a) - All contracts and/or agreements shall be in writing, shall be awarded on the basis 
of a competitive bid, and shall not exceed five (5) years in duration, and shall impose no penalties or 
surrender charges for the transfer of any asset(s) or responsibilities on expiration of the contract or 
agreement.
9. Section 9003.5(b) - You will not permit any other Trustee, Administrative Service Agency, Financial 
Organization, independent consultant or person to provide services in respect to the Model Plan we 
have adopted.

Plan Administration RFP
8
10. Section 9003.7 - You will not permit an investment of any amount, in any annuity contract providing 
for a term which could exceed five (5) years or which is measured by one or more natural lives or any 
life insurance or other contract providing traditional death benefits.
11. Section 9004.1 - All information obtained by your position will remain confidential and you will neither 
solicit nor provide products other than deferred compensation.
12. Section 9005.3 - Statements to participants will be provided quarterly, even in situations where no 
contributions are being made but funds are on deposit. You also agree to provide, at least annually, 
an additional statement to participants disclosing all fees and expenses paid out of or charged against 
plan assets.
13. Section 9005.4 - Agree to satisfy the bonding and insurance requirements of this Section and provide 
evidence of such.
14. Section 9006.2 - You agree to include in your contracts and agreements a provision that the contracts 
and agreements are subject to the Regulations and the Model Plan and that such Regulations and 
the Model Plan are made part thereof.
Specifications of the Model Plan
1. Section 3.2(a) - The Model Plan requires a minimum deferral amount to be $260 for any plan year. 
Your proposal will state this minimum requirement wherever requested.
2. Section 4.1 - You acknowledge that the amounts of compensation deferred by the participants will be 
invested, according to the participant’s investment directions, no later than two (2) business days 
following receipt thereof, in the appropriate investment funds.
3. Section 4.7(a) - The entire value of each participant’s account, including any annuities will be set 
aside and held by the trustee, in trust, and that your contracts and agreements will recognize and 
reflect such.

Plan Administration RFP
9
SECTION II
TRUSTEE SERVICES
NOTE: You may skip this section entirely if you are not a Financial Organization bidding to become 
Trustee. You do not need to copy any of the questions. Move to next applicable Section.
Section 9002.1(a) of the Regulations states that assets must be held by one or more trustees pursuant 
to one or more trust agreements. Such agreements must satisfy all the requirements of Section 
9002.1(b). Section 9002.1(b) also indicates who may be trustee. We reserve the right to create our own 
trust as provided by this Section 9002.1(b) but desire to explore the alternative of a Financial Organization 
acting as trustee.
Please respond to each of the following statements if you desire to be considered as trustee. If any 
statement does not apply, please indicate so by responding: "Not Applicable".
Requested Information
1. The name of your firm, address, name of primary contact person and telephone number.
2. Whether your firm has provided trust services to any New York State municipality for their Code 
Section 457(b) deferred compensation plan. List names of all such municipalities.
3. Description of trust services you would provide acting as a Financial Organization rendering only trust 
services. Please specify all fees, expenses, charges and costs for the trustee services. Please 
provide disclosure of any compensation structure.
4. If you are selected as the Financial Organization acting as our trustee and desire to additionally 
respond to performing the duties of an Administrative Service Agency, as described in Sections 
9000.2(b)(1) and 9002.1(b)(4) of the Regulations, please indicate your intention here.
5. If you respond affirmatively, then it will be necessary for you to complete the questions in Sections III 
and IV addressed to the Administrative Service Agency proposer. However, in addition to stating 
your intention to bid, it is requested that you indicate here the effect this will have on any fees, 
expenses, charges and costs as distinguished from those previously stated in this Section.
6. The trustee will also be requested to acknowledge in writing that it is a fiduciary with respect to all 
administrative or investment matters for which it has assumed responsibility as outlined in Section 
9002.2(a)(6) and 9003.6 of the Regulations.
7. Referring to Section 9005.4 of the Regulations, describe the type of bond and its limits that you will 
be furnishing. Include “cost disclosure” if it is your intention for us to satisfy any part of this obligation. 
8. Do you intend to supply us with a sample trust agreement for our consideration? If so, do you attest 
that this agreement meets all of the requirements applicable to trusts as stated in Section 9002.1(b) 
of the Regulations and Section 457(g) of the Code.
9. Do you agree that you may not assign or permit any other Trustee to act on your behalf for the 
activities/services you are contracted for?
10. What performance guarantees would you be willing to consider for this service?
SECTION III

Plan Administration RFP
10
ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICE AGENCY/
FINANCIAL ORGANIZATION
(Excluding Trustee)
Please respond to each of the following statements if you desire to be considered as either the 
Administrative Service Agency and/or the Financial Organization. If you feel any statement does not 
apply, please indicate so by responding: "Not Applicable" and provide your reasoning.
Company Background
1. The name of your firm, home office address, New York State address (if any), and the name (including 
title), address and phone number of your primary contact person whom we may contact about your 
proposal.
2. Give a very brief description of your company and its history of participation in similar public employee 
Code Section 457(b) deferred compensation plans for state and local government employers, 
including how many years your company has been providing these services. In New York State such 
plans first materialized in 1985, include your specific experience in similar plans in New York since 
that time.
3. How many public employee elective deferral retirement plans and deferred compensation plans do 
you currently provide administrative services and/or investment products for? How many of these 
plans are New York plans? 
4. In the past five (5) years has any public employee Code Section 457(b) deferred compensation 
plan/program, regardless of geographic location, terminated your (parent, subsidiary or affiliate) 
services either through the competitive bid process or for cause? If so, by whom and under what 
circumstances?
5. List ten (10) client Code Section 457(b) deferred compensation plan references for which your 
organization provides services and/or investment products similar to those requested in this proposal. 
It would be preferable if five (5) of the references could represent similar size clients to Monroe County 
(based on assets) from New York State, if possible. Please include contact person name, title, 
address and telephone number, number of participants, annual deferral amounts and approximate 
size of plan assets and the number of years you have been providing services. Spreadsheet format 
preferred.
6. What professional liability coverages are maintained by your company for errors and omissions or 
any other act?
7. Please provide an audited financial statement for the most recently completed fiscal year.
8. Please indicate if your firm has a SAS 70 report or an equivalent process to provide us assurance of 
the design and effectiveness of your internal controls.
9. Has your company been involved in any litigation in the last five (5) years or is there any pending 
litigation arising out of your performance or participation in a deferred compensation plan? If so, 
please provide a detailed explanation.

Plan Administration RFP
11
10. Financial Organization’s should provide appropriate “ratings” from the following: A.M. Best, Standard 
& Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch (formerly Duff & Phelps). Has your rating in any of these agencies fallen 
below “A-“ in the last five (5) years. If yes, give complete details. If, as a Financial Organization, you 
have no ratings by any of these agencies, please explain. 
11. What performance guarantees would you be willing to consider for this service?
12. Concisely provide any additional information that would distinguish your firm.

Plan Administration RFP
12
SECTION IV
SERVICES
Please respond to each of the following statements if you desire to be considered as the Administrative 
Service Agency. If you feel any statement does not apply, please indicate so by responding: "Not 
Applicable" and provide your reasoning. 
Marketing, Enrollment and Education Services
1. Briefly describe the marketing and employee communication strategy which will be used with our 
plan. Indicate the use and capabilities of laptop computers, if utilized. 
2. Briefly describe the types of marketing/promotional materials to be utilized. How will you work to 
develop a marketing program unique to our needs? To what extent can the material be branded to 
our plan?
3. Do you provide communications to participants on a regular basis, if so, please describe and provide 
samples?
4. Will these services and materials be prepared and distributed at your cost?
5. What educational materials will be provided to the Plan to maintain compliance?
6. Briefly describe how you propose to conduct group enrollment meetings and ongoing educational 
sessions so that all interested employees have an opportunity to attend at a convenient time and 
location, including monthly new employee orientations. How often are these type sessions proposed? 
Indicate the use and capabilities of laptop computers, if used.
7. Please describe, in detail, your one-on-one education sessions. Your response should emphasize
how you plan to satisfy “the individual one-on-one on demand availability” of your enrollment specialist 
especially at times and locations convenient to our employees.
8. What educational services are provided for retirees?
9. Describe your approach to asset allocation and diversification.
10. How do you follow-up with or contact employees that did not have an opportunity to attend a group 
session or with an employee subsequently hired after that meeting date? Your comments on the 
one-on-one availability of your enrollment specialists for this function are important. 
11. Briefly describe your continuing education program, if any.
12. Do you attest that these Enrollment Services are provided only by a properly licensed representative: 
licensed to meet both Federal and New York State requirements?
13. Describe the training, background, specialized knowledge and skills your company’s representatives 
must possess or attain. What services will these people provide other than the enrollment of 
participants?

Plan Administration RFP
13
14. Will enrollment and educational services proposed by your company be performed by your own 
employees? If no, provide the name, address and qualifications of each organization or individual that 
your company either has contracted or intends to contract for such services. If agents and not 
employees, so indicate.
15. How are your enroller representatives compensated, salary or commission? If commission is paid, 
does it vary according to the investment options selected?
16. How do you monitor enrollers’ performance during the initial enrollment and subsequent years?
17. List each enroller’s name, date of hire and at least one Deferred Compensation case currently being 
enrolled by this enroller.
18. What precautions will be in place to ensure that enrollers abide by Regulation Section 9004.1 which 
prohibits a service provider from soliciting or inducing plan participants to purchase or utilize products 
“for any purpose not directly related to the plan”?
19. What performance guarantees would you be willing to consider for this service?
Administrative Services
A. Services offered to the Plan Sponsor
1. Do you offer a dedicated toll-free Plan Sponsor line?
2. How does your organization provide assistance with revisions to the New York State Model 
Plan Document?
3. Does your company provide loans to participants? If so, is EFT repayment an available option?
4. Does your company administer ROTH 457 accounts? If so, how do you educate participants 
on the difference between a ROTH 457 and a ROTH 401(K)?
5. Will your company withhold, remit and report income taxes deducted from distributions? Does 
this service include the production and distribution all income tax reports to all the necessary 
parties as required by federal and state laws?
6. Specify all reports which will be issued to us, our participants and governmental agencies. 
B. Services offered to Participants
1. Describe any on-line investment guidance you propose to offer to plan participants. Describe 
any “Managed Account” services you propose to offer, if any.
2. Describe any enhanced features you propose to offer to high account balance plan participants 
to assist with their financial planning.
3. Describe your voice response telephone system. Identify all available services including 
customer service options as well as “Voice Response Systems” or automated options. Include 
security features and voice options, if applicable.
4. Can your customer service representatives assist non-English speaking participants?

Plan Administration RFP
14
5. Describe your internet strategy. What features are currently available on your website? What 
services are you developing for the near future? What security safeguards are used?
6. How often do you propose to distribute printed/mailed account balance statements?
7. Please describe the settlement options available to each participant at retirement, voluntary 
termination and death. Please state your compliance to reflect the Board’s continued 
prohibition on annuity distribution options (Section 9001.4 of the Regulations).
8. In the event you are asked to administer our plan alongside another provider(s), please 
describe your required process for assisting with participant requests to transfer plan assets 
from your program to one of the other carriers. Describe in detail the forms, signatures and 
overall process that you require. 
Recordkeeping System
1. Specify the basic recordkeeping system to be provided for our plan, with particular reference to the 
ability to receive, disburse, control and audit deductions, and to ensure timeliness, accuracy and 
confidentially of records and describe the software used.
2. Briefly describe data processing operations, including the media by which your company can receive 
payroll deduction information, and its security provisions. Include a statement about your disaster 
recovery plan and its site location. Identify any subcontracting requirements for your primary 
administration responsibilities and comment on how this is possible in light of Section 9003.5(b) of 
the Regulations.
3. Indicate all interfacing: payroll deduction inputs, required certifications and any other transactions, 
specifying all direct and indirect costs. Specify how payroll deduction information is to be supplied. 
Indicate ability to interface with internal data processing systems.
Fees and Expenses for Services
Please specify all fees, expenses, charges and costs for services provided under this Section, and 
whether they will vary and/or increase if you also provide trustee services as outlined in Section II if this 
RFP. Please also specify if they will vary and/or increase if you must also pay (1) the annual audit of the 
Plan, (2) Legal expenses of the Committee, (3) the incidental expenses of the Committee, including 
Committee Member education expenses.
To fund the fees, expenses, charges, and costs for services provided, please propose comparative 
revenue generating options of investment fund revenue sharing and per participant charges. For revenue 
sharing, please describe options for the disposition of revenue sharing in excess plan expenses. Does 
your firm offer a method of crediting account holders with a share of the revenue sharing?

Plan Administration RFP
15
SECTION V
INVESTMENTS
 
Please respond to each of the following statements if you desire to be considered as the Financial 
Organization. If you feel any statement does not apply, please indicate so by responding: "Not 
Applicable" and provide your reasoning.
Fund Offerings
Information should be for the most recent calendar quarter completed.
1. Describe fully the various attributes of each investment option your company has to offer. Please 
indicate whether your company is proposing a variable annuity product, mutual fund investment or 
other. For each option include an Investment Options Summary sheet which includes the funds 
objective, portfolio statistics, asset allocation, top 10 holdings, and industry diversification. Please 
also provide samples of specimen investment contracts and prospectuses for each and every 
investment option your company proposes.
2. Describe fully your “fixed” investment option. Include a one-page summary including applicable rates 
for the last five (5) calendar years, asset composition, and rating methodology. When does your 
company anticipate changing its credited interest rate(s) and to what extent, and with what frequency?
Please also include a breakdown of all expenses for this product, including an estimate of revenue 
received by your firm in excess of the surrender rate.
3. Illustrate in spreadsheet format provided, (see Exhibit A) the "variable" values for each equity type 
investment. Please give annualized returns for ‘year-to-date’, ‘one year’, ‘three year’, ‘five year’ ‘ten 
year’ and ‘since inception’ values.
4. Illustrate in spreadsheet format provided, (see Exhibit B) all charges including loading costs, policy 
fees, surrender charges, actuarial margins, asset fees, transfer charges, distribution charges, 
withdrawal fees, redemption fees, commission, termination/withdrawal of contract fees, etc., etc.
5. You must agree to set up an alternative plan to Social Security for part-time/seasonal employees 
(OBRA) within the 457 plan at no cost to the Plan and must agree to provide all documents, 
administration, paperwork and other services normally associated with this plan. Please provide full 
details of the type(s) of investment option(s) you will be able to offer part-time/seasonal employees 
who select this option.

Plan Administration RFP
3
GENERAL INFORMATION
Background
The Monroe County Deferred Compensation Plan (the Plan) is a defined contribution plan covering all 
the employees of the County of Monroe. The Plan is exempt from income taxes under Internal Revenue 
Service Section 457(b) of the Internal Revenue Code. The Plan is subject to the Rules and Regulations 
of the New York State Deferred Compensation Board, Parts 9000 to 9006 and operates off of the State 
Model Plan Document.
The purpose of the Plan is to provide employees with a convenient and efficient way to build long-term 
retirement savings and to encourage broad-based participation of employees in the plan as a 
supplemental retirement security tool to their State defined benefit pension and Social Security. The Plan 
wants to assure that this additional benefit be recognized by all employees, that they have the opportunity 
to receive one-on-one education and voluntarily participate.
The Plan also has an OBRA part time seasonal component.
As of December 31, 2022, the Plan had 4,398 plan participants with a Plan assets of $308,676,730. In 
addition the OBRA part-time seasonal plan had 536 participants with assets of $926,785. Contributions 
were $13,290,747 during the year, plus roll over inflow. The median account balance was $26,191. 
Additional Plan information is presented in Exhibit C. The County currently has approximately 4,100 full-time employees at any given time. The Plan is supported by one (1) full-time exclusive enroller/educator. 
He conducts approximately 100 group meetings and over 1,000 individual seminars.
County’s Objective
The County’s objectives in seeking to maintain such a plan for its employees are as follows:
1. To provide a means by which its employees can enhance their financial position and retirement 
income.
2. To provide a planned program that will facilitate their efforts to do so.
3. To provide a system for a social security compliance program for seasonal and part-time employment.
4. To provide consultation on an as-needed basis for review of financial hardship withdrawal.
5. To provide a trustee to meet trustee requirement as per the Rules and Regulations established by 
the New York State Deferred Compensation Board. 
6. To assist the Monroe County Deferred Compensation Committee in the performance of its duties 
under Section 41 of the Monroe County Code and to implement the decision of the committee.

Plan Administration RFP
4
Scope of Services
The Monroe County Deferred Compensation Plan Committee (the Committee) developed this Request 
For Proposals (RFP) to obtain proposals from qualified Administrative Service Agencies and/or Financial 
Organizations relating to (1) trust service, (2) administration and/or (3) funding of an "eligible deferred 
compensation plan.” If you are "qualified" according to the Regulations to administer, maintain records 
and accounts of plans and/or if you have appropriate trust services and/or products available for use as 
funding media and are interested in making those services and/or products available, you are requested 
to complete this RFP.
Submission of Proposal
1. Six (6) copies plus one original of the proposal should be submitted to the following address to arrive
no later than 3:00 p.m. on September 8, 2023:
Walter Webert, Contract Management Coordinator
Monroe County Deferred Compensation Committee
c/o County of Monroe
Office of Purchasing & Central Services
39 W. Main Street, Room 200
Rochester, NY 14614
2. Questions that arise during the proposal preparation process must be received in writing, or via e-mail, by Walter Webert no later than 3:00 P.M. on August 18, 2023 (e-mail: 
wwebert@monroecounty.gov). Questions and responses will be provided in the form of an addendum 
to the specifications which, if issued, will be conveyed via e-mail to all firms who received this RFP 
no later than the close of business August 25, 2023. No contact will be allowed between the firm and 
any other member of the Committee or County with regard to this RFP during the RFP process unless 
specifically authorized in writing by the Contract Management Coordinator or his designee. Prohibited 
contact may be grounds for firm disqualification.
3. Any proposals received after 3:00 p.m. on September 8, 2023 will not be considered. It is each 
Proposer’s responsibility to assure that proposals are shipped in a timely fashion so as to be received 
by the designated party on or before the due date. We accept no responsibility for lost and/or late 
delivery of proposals.
Form and Substance
The New York State Deferred Compensation Board has promulgated The "Rules and Regulations" 
(effective June 15, 2011), hereafter referred to as the "Regulations", and the Model Plan (including 
amendments through December 11, 2020) for which you are to rely on for responding to this RFP. These 
documents can be found at the following link: https://deferredcompboard.ny.gov
Failure to conform to or satisfy any requirement of these documents may result in the rejection of the 
proposal. 
1. Proposer must include a fully completed questionnaire, restating each statement or question in 
Section I through Section V inclusive, and by recording your response directly below each statement 
or question.

Plan Administration RFP
5
2. Proposers must respond to all questions in the "Contractual Requirements" section (Section I) and 
must conform to the specifications set forth in this RFP. If a question, statement or section does not 
apply, put “not applicable” as your response. If recordkeeping services are provided by a “person” 
(defined by the Regulations) that is neither the parent nor subsidiary company of the Financial 
Organization, then separate and complete responses must be provided by each company.
3. Proposer must include a transmittal letter on the Company's official letterhead signed by an official of 
the Company who is authorized to commit the organization to perform the services outlined in the 
submitted proposal: you must indicate such commitment. The transmittal letter must contain a 
representation that the proposal complies with all requirements of the Regulations and the Model 
Plan. 
4. By submitting a proposal, each Proposer agrees not to make any claims for or have any right to 
damages because of any misunderstanding or misrepresentation of specifications, because of any 
misinformation or lack of information or because such Proposer is not selected to provide the services 
proposed. Submission of a proposal constitutes express acceptance by the Proposer of all provisions 
of this RFP including all attachments.
5. By submitting a proposal, you agree to include in your contracts and agreements a provision that all 
commitments, representations, promises or claims made in your proposal documents or oral 
presentations are made part of any contract entered into with the Committee.

the guidelines set forth in this RFP. All responses should be as concise as possible. Excessive 
submissions may be grounds for disqualification.
Evaluation Criteria
In selecting, we will use criteria which comply with the requirements of the Regulations, including Section 
9003.3(a)(1 through 7) of the Regulations.
All qualified proposals, sought in conjunction with the requirements of Section 9003.2 of the Regulations, 
will be evaluated and awards made to the Proposer or Proposers whose bid is determined to be in the 
best interest of the plan participants.
Selection Process
Section 9001.2(b) of the Regulations, recognizes that we have appointed a committee to act on our 
behalf, to the extent permitted or required by the Regulations and by the Model Plan. Section 9003.3(c): 
before any contract or agreement entered into by the committee may become effective, the committee 
must submit in writing, to the President of the New York State Civil Service Commission, the name of 
such selected Proposer(s) and a “certification” signed by the chief executive officer and chief legal officer 
stating that such Proposer(s) has been duly selected to provide services in accordance with provisions 
of the Regulations.

notwithstanding, we reserve the right at any time to:
a. reject any or all proposals or parts thereof;
b. establish a deferred compensation plan by any of the methods prescribed by Section
